quests.question: The theater, ___ the play premiered a century ago, still hosts live performances today.
quests.hint: This clause just adds extra detail about an already-identified theater, and the play premiered IN it.
quests.explanation: Commas signal a non-defining clause, so 'that' cannot be used; 'in which' follows the preposition 'in' for a thing.

quests.question: ___ wrote the score for that play went on to become a celebrated composer.
quests.hint: The missing word means 'any person who' - the identity of that composer is unspecified here.
quests.explanation: 'Whoever' means 'any person who,' used because the composer is not identified by name.

quests.question: That playwright ___ final work premiered posthumously never saw the audience's reaction.
quests.hint: The final work belongs to the playwright - which pronoun shows possession?
quests.explanation: 'Whose' shows that the final work belongs to the playwright being described.

quests.question: The trail, on ___ hikers often get lost, now has new trail markers every mile.
quests.hint: This clause just adds extra detail about an already-identified trail, and hikers get lost ON it.
quests.explanation: Commas signal a non-defining clause, so 'that' cannot be used; 'on which' follows the preposition 'on' for a thing.

quests.question: Construction crews rerouted the trail around the fallen trees, ___ added nearly two miles to the hike.
quests.hint: The missing word refers to the whole situation - the rerouting - not one noun.
quests.explanation: 'Which' refers to the entire preceding action, not a single noun, so 'that' cannot be used here.

quests.question: Some hikers ___ the summit at sunrise said the view was worth every step.
quests.hint: This is a shortened relative clause with 'who were' removed - only the '-ing' form remains.
quests.explanation: A reduced relative clause drops 'who were' and keeps only the '-ing' form: 'reaching.'

quests.question: The professor, to ___ I owe my entire interest in this subject, still emails me articles.
quests.hint: You owe your interest TO this professor - which pronoun form follows a preposition for a person?
quests.explanation: 'To whom' is correct because a preposition directly precedes the pronoun, requiring the object form 'whom.'

quests.question: ___ made her lectures so memorable was how personally she told every story.
quests.hint: This word means 'the thing that' and starts the sentence, acting as its own subject.
quests.explanation: 'What' means 'the thing that' and functions as the subject of this sentence.

quests.question: We still talk about the professors and the courses ___ shaped our whole career.
quests.hint: The clause covers both people AND things together - which pronoun works for both?
quests.explanation: 'That' can refer to a mix of people and things, while 'who' only works for people and 'which' only for things.

quests.question: The garden, ___ my mother spent countless hours, still blooms every single spring.
quests.hint: This clause just adds extra detail about an already-identified garden, and she spent hours IN it.
quests.explanation: Commas signal a non-defining clause, so 'that' cannot be used; 'in which' follows the preposition 'in' for a thing.

quests.question: A neighbor ___ my mother taught to garden still brings us vegetables every summer.
quests.hint: Who did the teaching? My mother did - so the neighbor is the object of 'taught.'
quests.explanation: Since 'my mother' is the subject of 'taught,' the neighbor is the object, so 'whom' is correct.

quests.question: She arranges the flowers ___ she wants; nobody has ever questioned her eye for design.
quests.hint: The missing word means 'in whatever way' - it describes an unspecified style of arranging.
quests.explanation: 'However' here means 'in whatever way' and describes an unspecified manner.

quests.question: The board, on ___ she has sat for three years, finally approved her proposal.
quests.hint: This clause just adds extra detail about an already-identified board, and she sits ON it.
quests.explanation: Commas signal a non-defining clause, so 'that' cannot be used; 'on which' follows the preposition 'on' for a thing.

quests.question: That board voted to extend her contract early, ___ surprised absolutely no one.
quests.hint: The missing word refers to the whole situation - the early vote - not one noun.
quests.explanation: 'Which' refers to the entire preceding action, not a single noun, so 'that' cannot be used here.

quests.question: This policy ___ during her first term is still in place today.
quests.hint: This is a shortened passive clause with 'that was' removed - only the past participle remains.
quests.explanation: A reduced passive relative clause drops 'that was' and keeps only the past participle: 'introduced.'

quests.question: The workshop, at ___ dozens of local artists have trained, celebrates its fortieth anniversary this year.
quests.hint: This clause just adds extra detail about an already-identified workshop, and artists trained AT it.
quests.explanation: Commas signal a non-defining clause, so 'that' cannot be used; 'at which' follows the preposition 'at' for a thing.

quests.question: ___ started this tradition decades ago probably never imagined it would still continue.
quests.hint: The missing word means 'any person who' - the identity of that founder is unspecified here.
quests.explanation: 'Whoever' means 'any person who,' used because the founder is not identified by name.

quests.question: This year's turnout was almost exactly the same size ___ last year's.
quests.hint: After 'the same,' one specific word is required to complete the comparison.
quests.explanation: 'As' is required after 'the same' to complete this type of comparison.

quests.question: The colleague, on ___ I have always been able to rely, is retiring at the end of the month.
quests.hint: You rely ON this colleague - which pronoun form follows a preposition for a person?
quests.explanation: 'On whom' is correct because a preposition directly precedes the pronoun, requiring the object form 'whom.'

quests.question: I never fully understood ___ made him so universally trusted by everyone in the office.
quests.hint: This word means 'the thing that' - there's no earlier noun for it to point back to.
quests.explanation: 'What' means 'the thing that' and introduces this clause without needing an earlier noun.

quests.question: He is genuinely the most reliable coworker ___ I have ever worked alongside.
quests.hint: After a superlative like 'the most reliable,' which pronoun sounds most natural?
quests.explanation: After superlatives, 'that' is the natural, idiomatic choice in everyday English.

quests.question: The village, ___ the festival has been held for generations, was completely transformed for the celebration.
quests.hint: This clause just adds extra detail about an already-identified village, and the festival is held IN it.
quests.explanation: Commas signal a non-defining clause, so 'that' cannot be used; 'in which' follows the preposition 'in' for a thing.

quests.question: A family ___ home hosted the very first festival still lives in the village today.
quests.hint: The home belongs to the family - which pronoun shows possession?
quests.explanation: 'Whose' shows that the home belongs to the family being described.

quests.question: Local elders ___ the old stories keep the town's history alive for every new generation.
quests.hint: This is a shortened relative clause with 'who' plus 'are' removed - only the '-ing' form remains.
quests.explanation: A reduced relative clause drops 'who are' and keeps only the '-ing' form: 'preserving.'

quests.question: The observatory, at ___ astronomers first confirmed the discovery, is now open to the public on weekends.
quests.hint: This clause just adds extra detail about an already-identified observatory, and astronomers confirmed it AT that place.
quests.explanation: Commas signal a non-defining clause, so 'that' cannot be used; 'at which' follows the preposition 'at' for a thing.

quests.question: That telescope captured images no one expected, ___ reshaped our understanding of the galaxy.
quests.hint: The missing word refers to the whole situation - capturing unexpected images - not one noun.
quests.explanation: 'Which' refers to the entire preceding event, not a single noun, so 'that' cannot be used here.

quests.question: Our research team set up new equipment ___ conditions allowed the clearest view of the sky.
quests.hint: The missing word means 'any place where' - it refers to an unspecified location.
quests.explanation: 'Wherever' means 'any place where' and is used for an unspecified location.

quests.question: The classroom, ___ she taught for thirty-five years, now bears a plaque with her name.
quests.hint: This final sentence combines everything you've learned: a non-defining clause with a fronted preposition, honoring a lifetime of teaching.
quests.explanation: Commas signal a non-defining clause, so 'that' cannot be used; 'in which' follows the preposition 'in' for a thing.

quests.question: ___ she gave her students was not just knowledge, but the confidence to keep asking questions.
quests.hint: This word means 'the thing that' and starts the sentence, acting as its own subject - the same pattern you first practiced many levels ago, now carrying real weight.
quests.explanation: 'What' means 'the thing that' and functions as the subject of this sentence, just as it has throughout this unit.

quests.question: ___ walks into that classroom today can still feel the quiet sense of purpose she left behind.
quests.hint: The missing word means 'any person who' - closing this whole journey the same way it began, with a single unknown person and one small word that carries the whole clause.
quests.explanation: 'Whoever' means 'any person who,' used because the visitor's identity is unknown - a fitting close to everything this course has covered.
